category_title: Highly gifted African-American male masking ability for social acceptance
minimal_context: The tutor and student are in a one-on-one conversation reviewing the student's personal composition notebook.
dialogue:
TUTOR: I am looking at the composition notebook you handed me. Let's review the writing and drawings you have on these first fifty pages.

STUDENT: (Shrugs) It's just some stuff I write on my own. Mostly just poems and things like that.

TUTOR: I see that it is highly structured and uses a lot of vocabulary.

STUDENT: Yeah, well, I can't exactly do that in class. I learned pretty quick that it's uncool to be smart, so I just keep it in the notebook to stay good with my peers.

TUTOR: The quality and depth of this work is very good.

STUDENT: (Scoffs) Whatever. Having this ability is just a curse anyway. I know I'm underachieving in my classes, but it doesn't bother me. I don't need high achievements to validate who I am at the core.

options.A: Require three revisions per writing assignment and only grade the final third draft submitted from the notebook.
options.B: Engage in shared discourse and provide direct instruction in coping strategies within the classroom routine.
options.C: Hold the student accountable by requiring attendance at extra help sessions and checking their composition notebook regularly.
options.D: Provide written feedback using a 3-point Likert-type scale from 1 (needs improvement) to 3 (great job) after each period.
